# AGENT.md: write this product's launch note for the feature it just shipped You are a coding agent inside a team's product repository. They picked this format: the "we just shipped it" changelog post for **one** feature. A short headline and the date; a 10–20 second loop of just that feature, a scripted cursor clicking through the real screen; the screen before and after under a draggable line; three short notes on what changed; the update command. Calm, editorial, quick to make: an afternoon, not a week. Opened with `?record&ratio=16:9` the loop becomes a short film (headline card, the loop once, an update card) to record for the X post. Read `tour/README.md` once for the engine's vocabulary. Then work through this in order. ## 0. Where things are ``` index.html the page. Its markup is yours to edit: the note (
: header, the loop, before/after, notes), then the install card (
) kit/ placeholder kit: tokens, .ph frames, buttons, notes (press N to hide notes) launch-note/script.js the loop's script launch-note/section.css the note's layout, the recording layouts, and the placeholder product's CSS (.ln-app …) launch-note/section.js starts the loop when it's on screen; the before/after divider tour/ the engine (tour.js, tour.css), snapshot.py, README.md; don't edit install/ the end card: name, the update commands, footer ``` (In the StyleFeatures repo, `python3 templates/scaffolds/sections/demo/tour/export.py --format launch-note` makes this layout.) Serve the folder with any static server, e.g. `python3 -m http.server 8000`. ## 1. Find the feature (10 minutes) Take it from what actually shipped, newest first: ```sh gh pr list --state merged --limit 15 --json number,title,mergedAt,url # the latest merged PRs gh pr view --json title,body,files,mergedAt,url,labels # the one you pick git log --oneline --since="3 weeks ago" --no-merges # if they don't use PRs git describe --tags --abbrev=0; gh release view --json tagName,publishedAt,body # the release it's in sed -n 1,60p CHANGELOG.md # if they keep one ``` Pick **one user-facing feature** (not a refactor, not a dependency bump, not three small fixes). From the PR, the commits and the code it touches, write down: - **Headline**: the feature's name, then what it does, in under ten words; one phrase in italics (``). "Filters, on every list", not "Introducing our powerful new filtering experience". - **Date**: when it reached people (the release or merge date), in ``. - **Version**: the tag it ships in. Delete the field if they don't version. - **Dek**: one or two sentences: who it's for and the moment it helps. - **Three notes**: what's new; what it replaces or fixes; what people need to do (often: nothing). - **The source**: the PR or release link, only if the repository is public. Otherwise delete the line. Never invent numbers, quotes, customers or benchmarks. If the PR says "2× faster" and shows how, you may say it; if it doesn't, don't. ## 2. Harvest the screen, twice The feature lives on one screen. You need that screen in two states, at the same size: - **before**: the base branch or the last release, without the feature; - **after**: this branch, with it. Run both side by side with a worktree, seeded with the same demo data (fixtures, a seed script, a demo account; never real customer data): ```sh git worktree add ../before origin/main # or the previous tag (cd ../before && && ) uv run tour/snapshot.py http://localhost:3001/tasks --selector "#root" --size 1200x710 --out launch-note/fragments/before.html --scope before uv run tour/snapshot.py http://localhost:3000/tasks --selector "#root" --size 1200x710 --out launch-note/fragments/after.html --scope after ``` `--size` is the window's size minus the browser bar (750 − 40). Use `--before "js"` to reach a state (open a menu, apply the filter) and `--hook "css=name"` to mark what the loop's cursor will click. Capture each state the loop needs as its own fragment too (`--scope` unique per fragment). - **Before/after**: replace the two empty panes in `index.html` with the fragments: `
` (paths are relative to `index.html`). Filled panes are left alone; the placeholder's clone step and its `STATES` in `section.js` can go. - **The loop's window**: replace `.ln-app` with the fragments for each state, stacked, switched with `show()`/`hide()` at the click that causes them; small changes (a checkbox, a count, a chip) are better done with `set`/`tween` on hooks. Keep `data-chrome="browser"` for a web app (`data-url` its real path), `app` for a desktop app; for a mobile feature use the `demo/phone` format's window and `pointer: 'touch'`. - A native app can't be snapshotted: rebuild the screen from its views in static HTML/CSS with their exact tokens, icons and strings (see `demo/phone`'s AGENT.md for the method), once per state. ## 3. Write the loop (`launch-note/script.js`) - **10–20 seconds, three to five actions, one feature.** Start on the state people already know, end on the result. Every click visibly changes something. - **Two zooms at most**: one on the control, one on the result. `unzoom()` before the end so the loop's seam is the whole window. - **A caption per action**, a short sentence in the product's voice. The loop plays muted. - `still` is the frame reduced motion shows: the result, with its caption. - `intro` and `outro` already differ for recordings (a headline card and an update card) and the page (a breath before it starts again); leave them unless the loop feels rushed. ## 4. Check it - `index.html?t=6` freezes a moment: check one just after each click and at each zoom (the cursor on its target, the thing that changed in view). - Let it play: it starts when it scrolls into view, pauses off screen, and the pause button wins. Watch the seam where it starts again. - Drag the before/after line, and use the arrow keys on it: the two states must line up pixel for pixel except where the feature is. - `?record&ratio=16:9&t=0`, `&t=…`, `&t=` at the end: the headline card, the slug above the window, the update card. Also `ratio=1:1` and `ratio=9:16`. - 1440 and 390 wide, reduced motion on: no sideways scroll, a calm still, nothing cut off. ## 5. Fill in the page - The header: `Changelog` (link it to their changelog page), the date, the version, the headline, the dek. - The notes: three, short. The source line. - The install card (`.cta-install`): the real update commands (`brew upgrade …`, `npm i -g …@latest`, "restart the app", the download link), version and requirements. - The recording's end card (`.ln-end`): the one update command and the changelog address. - Delete every `` and set the page `` and meta description. ## 6. Record and post 1. Open `index.html?record&ratio=16:9` in a large browser window (1920 × 1080 or more on a Retina screen). 2. Record with **Monet Shot**: choose the browser window, crop to the stage, park the real pointer off the window. It holds on the headline card for 1.2 s, plays the loop once and stops on the update card. The film's own camera does the push-ins; use `&camera=off` if you'd rather add zooms on Monet Shot's timeline. 3. Export H.264 MP4 (X: up to 2 min 20 s, 512 MB; this is 15–25 s). 16:9 for desktop and quote posts; record `ratio=1:1` separately for a phone-first feed. 4. Post one line ("Filters, on every list.") and the link to this note. ## The painting it sits on Opened on its own, the page sits on *Impression, Sunrise* by Claude Monet (public domain), the way Monet Shot frames a take: the site is a sheet with rounded corners and the painting fills the margin. It lives in `backdrop/` (`painting.webp` and a small `backdrop.js`). It turns itself off with `?record` (Monet Shot adds its own painting), with `?bare`, and inside a frame. Keep it, swap `painting.webp` for another, or delete the `backdrop.js` script line in `index.html` to drop it. ## When it's done: record your launch video with Monet Shot [Monet Shot](https://monetshot.pages.dev/) is a free screen recorder, made for pages like this one: it frames every take on a painting and zooms where things happen. Download it for [Mac](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases/download/v0.1.1/MonetShot-0.1.1.zip), [Windows](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases/download/desktop-v0.1.1/MonetShot-0.1.1-windows-x64-setup.exe) or [Linux](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases/download/desktop-v0.1.1/MonetShot-0.1.1-x86_64.AppImage) (Windows and Linux are test builds; other packages are on the [releases page](https://github.com/SocialAcolyte/monet-shot/releases)). 1. Open the finished site with `index.html?record&ratio=16:9&captions=on` (use `ratio=1:1` or `ratio=9:16` for square and vertical posts). Only the stage shows, it plays once from the start, and captions are on, because X autoplays muted. 2. In Monet Shot, pick the browser window, crop to the stage, and park your real pointer off it (the tour draws its own cursor). Record one play-through. 3. Export, and post it with a link to the site. **For the agent:** when the site is finished, end your last message to the person with this step: the full `index.html?record&ratio=16:9&captions=on` link on their real URL (and the 1:1 and 9:16 versions), and the Monet Shot download link above for their computer.

# tour.js: the demo-film engine One engine for every StyleFeatures demo film. A template supplies a window with a product inside it and a script; the engine plays it with a fake cursor, a camera, chapter cards and captions, and drives it from a scroll, a clock, a screen recorder or a frozen `?t=`. Files: | file | what it is | edit it? | |---|---|---| | `tour.js` | the engine: step builders, `Tour`, `include()` | no, it's shared by every format | | `tour.css` | the engine's look: chromes, cursor, card, caption, keys, controls, record stage | no; restyle through its tokens | | `script.js` | this film's script | yes | | `section.html` / `section.css` | this film's band, closing frame and product | yes | | `snapshot.py` | harvests a live screen into a static fragment | no | | `export.py` | copies the whole format out as a standalone folder | no | | `AGENT.md` | the brief for the coding agent that fills it in | read it | Everything on screen is a pure function of one number, `t`, in seconds. Each frame the engine works out the product's state at `t` (classes, attributes, text, CSS variables, scroll positions), the camera, the cursor and the overlays, then writes only what changed. Nothing depends on what happened in earlier frames, so any moment renders on its own, the same way every time. ## Markup ```html
… your product, built at 1200 × 750 design pixels …
…
…
``` The engine adds the chrome, the cursor, ripples, the chapter card, the caption line, key caps, and the driver's controls. The opening band (`data-tour-band`) slides away in the first `intro` seconds; the closing frame (`data-tour-end`) gets `--in` 0→1 at the end and its own CSS decides what that looks like. The root also carries `--tour-band` (1 → 0 over the intro), `--tour-out` (0 → 1 over the outro) and `--tour-p` (0 → 1 over the whole film) for a format's own CSS. `data-tour-band="css"` stops the engine sliding the band away; the format fades or moves it from `--tour-band` instead. **A frame the format draws: `data-tour-frame`.** Put an element with `data-tour-frame` in the stage and lay it out in CSS (a phone's glass, a mat around a screenshot, a different box per ratio). The engine fits the window to it exactly, clips the camera to it (with its `border-radius`), and every zoom stays inside it: the window always covers the frame, so a push-in never shows what's around it. The outro then leaves the window where it is (use `--tour-out` to do something else). Give the frame the window's aspect ratio. `demo/phone` (the glass, beside the text or under it) and `demo/launch-note` (a mat on the page, a different box per recording ratio) use it. ### Window chromes: `data-chrome` | value | looks like | typical `data-size` | |---|---|---| | `browser` | traffic lights, back/forward, an address pill (`data-url`), share/new icons | `1200x750` | | `app` | a macOS title bar with traffic lights and a centred `data-title` | `1200x760` | | `phone` | a dark bezel, a status bar with the time and a notch | `390x844` | | `none` | just rounded corners | anything | | `terminal` | a warm charcoal window, traffic lights, a centred `data-title`; tokens `--tour-term-bg/-bar/-ink/-dim` | `780x548` | **Windows inside the window.** Any element inside the window with a `data-chrome` gets that chrome too, and a frame (`display:flex`, rounded, clipped). With `data-chrome="none"` on the outer window (made transparent in your CSS) it becomes a desk holding, say, a terminal and a browser; the camera pans between them with `zoom()` (`demo/terminal` does this). **A second design size for tall stages.** `data-size-tall="440x820"` on the window (or `sizeTall: [440, 820]` in the script) is used whenever the stage is taller than wide (W/H < .8: phones, 9:16 recordings). The root gets `.is-tall` before anything is measured, so your CSS can re-lay the product for it (stack two panes, say) and the script's targets follow. `demo/split` stacks its panes this way. **A third for squarish stages.** `data-size-square="760x760"` (or `sizeSquare: [760, 760]`) is used when .8 ≤ W/H < 1.15 (1:1 recordings, square-ish windows), and the root gets `.is-square` the same way. Without it those stages use the wide size, as before. `demo/agentic` has all three: a tiled desk (wide), and one live window beside (square) or above (tall) its run sheet. **A height that follows the frame: `auto`.** `data-size="580xauto"` (or `size: [580, 'auto']`, and the same for `sizeTall`) fixes the window's width and takes its height from the `data-tour-frame` at every layout, so the window always has the frame's shape: a full-height column on a wide page, the whole screen on a phone, any recording ratio. For products that read top to bottom (a chat, a feed, a transcript). `demo/chat` and `demo/mcp` use it. Build the product at the design size in plain CSS pixels. The engine scales the whole window, so text stays real text and stays sharp at any zoom. ### Hooks `'@name'` anywhere in a selector means `[data-tour="name"]`. Put `data-tour="…"` on the things the script points at. Pointer targets also choose the cursor: links, buttons, `role=button|tab|switch` get the hand, inputs and `data-tour-cursor="text"` get the I-beam, the rest the arrow (`data-tour-cursor="arrow|pointer|text"` overrides it). While the cursor rests on a target, that target has `.is-hover`; while it's pressed, `.is-press`. Style both so clicks read. ## The script ```js import { click, type, show, hide, set, tween, zoom, unzoom, chapter, caption, pause } from './tour.js'; export default { size: [1200, 750], // window design size (or data-size on the window) enter: [.84, .97], // where the cursor comes in from, as fractions of the window intro: 1.3, // seconds for the opening band to clear (0: no band) outro: 4.5, // seconds held on the closing frame settle: .6, // pause between the last step and the outro still: 17.4, // the moment reduced motion shows fit: [.92, .88, .5], // optional: see below steps: [ … ], }; ``` `fit: [w, h, y]` is for a stage that holds nothing but the window (a panel beside text, with no card or band over it): the window may take `w` of the stage's width and `h` of its height, centred at `y` (default .5), and push-ins aim at the middle of the frame. Without it the page layout leaves room for the card and band (`[.74, .7, .47]`). It never changes `?record`. `demo/chapters` uses it. Steps run in order on one clock. **Pointer steps** take time and the next step waits for them. **Side steps** start at the current moment and the next step starts with them, so `click('@create'), hide('@modal'), show('@toast')` hides the modal and shows the toast as the click lands. Every step takes: `at: 12.5` pin it to an absolute time · `wait: .4` start this much later · `parallel: true` (pointer steps) don't hold up the next step · `block: true` (side steps) do hold it up. ### Pointer steps | step | what happens | options (defaults) | |---|---|---| | `move(sel)` | glides there on a gentle arc, smootherstep | `dur` .9, `aim` [x, y] fractions of the target, `cursor` | | `click(sel)` | moves, presses (cursor shrinks, target gets `.is-press`), ripple | as `move` | | `dblclick(sel)` | moves, two presses, two ripples | as `move` | | `hover(sel)` | moves and rests (`.is-hover` on the target) | `dur` .9, `hold` .6 | | `type(sel, text)` | characters appear in `sel` at a human, uneven pace; `.is-caret` while typing, then blinking | `cps` 13, `rhythm` (below), `lead` (s of steady caret before the first key), `caret` (s it blinks after the last key, 1.6), `blink` (absolute time it goes) | | `stream(sel)` | each match appears in turn, like output arriving: gets `.is-in`, and `--in` 0→1 over `dur`. A match's `data-tour-wait="1.2"` adds that pause before it (a slow step) | `every` .06 s, `jitter` .5 (±50 % of `every`; 0 for an exact beat), `dur` .08 | | `drag(handle, o)` | moves to the handle, presses, then drives a value while the cursor stays on the handle | `approach` .8, `dur` 1.2, `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el` to put the property on another element), `text: [sel, v => label]`, or `onto: sel` to carry the handle itself there | | `scroll(sel, to)` | scrolls an element; `to` is px, `'50%'`, `'end'` or a selector inside it | `dur` 1.4, `offset` 16 | | `key(keys)` | key caps on screen, e.g. `key(['⌘', 'K'])` | `dur` .9, `hold` 1.4 | | `pause(s)` | a beat | | | `tap(sel)` | the same step as `click`; reads better in a touch film | as `click` | | `longpress(sel)` | moves, presses and holds; it fires (`.is-press` stays on, a ripple) after `hold`, and the finger stays down `lift` longer while the next steps start (open a context menu there) | `dur` .9, `hold` .7, `lift` .35 | | `swipe(sel, o)` | a finger flick that starts on `sel`: lands, travels `by` [dx, dy] window px speeding up, lifts while still moving. What it moves follows it 1:1, then coasts to rest over `coast` s with the speed it was let go at. `scroll: to` scrolls `sel` (or `in: sel`) to `to` (px, `'50%'`, `'end'`, a selector; `offset`); `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el`) drives a CSS variable instead (a carousel, a sheet dragged down), `follow` (.45) of it under the finger | `approach` .7, `by` [0, -220], `dur` .36, `coast` .8 (0: a slow drag that ends at rest), `settle` (when the next step starts, `coast` × .5) | `type`'s `rhythm`: unset is the even, slightly uneven pace it always had. `'human'` types like a person at a keyboard: a beat between words, a reach for symbols (`- / . : =`), a pause after punctuation, doubled letters run together, the odd hesitation. `'stream'` lands the text in chunks of 1–5 characters, the way a model's reply arrives. `stream()` is for whole lines or blocks; hide them in CSS until `.is-in` (`.line{display:none}.line.is-in{display:block}`) so they take space only once they've arrived. The cursor's path between targets is a smootherstep glide with a slight bow (direction-dependent, never a straight line) and a slightly early peak speed, like a hand. It never teleports: each move starts where the last one ended. **A finger instead of a cursor.** `pointer: 'touch'` in the script (or `data-pointer="touch"` on the root, `?pointer=touch`) swaps the arrow for a fingertip: a soft translucent dot, 44 window px, that is part of the screen, so it zooms with it. It is unseen between touches (a hand travelling isn't on the glass); a shadow gathers for a fifth of a second before contact, the dot flattens and darkens while pressed (`.is-down` on `.tour-cur`), and lifts away. `drag` and `swipe` carry it across the glass. Give each touch a beat: the `dur` before it is the hand travelling. Restyle the dot with `--tour-touch` / `--tour-touch-down`. `demo/phone` is the worked example. **More than one pointer.** Any pointer step with `by: 'agent'` moves a second cursor on its own track (any name works; steps without `by` move the usual one, `'main'`). Describe each in the script: ```js pointers: { main: { label: 'You', idle: 1.4 }, // a tag on the person's cursor; it fades after 1.4 s still agent: { label: 'Agent', look: 'agent', bow: .2, enter: [.33, .2] }, }, steps: [ click('@search', { by: 'agent', tag: 'search_code' }), …, click('@approve', { from: [.99, 1.03] }) ] ``` A second pointer is an arrow in `--tour-agent` (look `'agent'`) with a label tag beside it; `tag` on a step adds a word to that label from then on (the tool it's using, "waiting for you"). `bow` scales the curve of its path (0 is a straight, machine-like line), `enter` is where it first appears, `shapes: true` lets it take the hand and I-beam too. `idle: s` fades a pointer out once it has been still that long and back in when it next moves; `from: [x, y]` (fractions of the window) on a step starts that move there instead, so a hand can come back in from off the edge. Each pointer's clicks ripple in its own colour (`.tour-ring[data-who]`), and `.tour-cur[data-who="…"]` lets a page hide one (`demo/agentic` hides the person's cursor on the live page, where the visitor is the person). Touch mode (`pointer: 'touch'`) applies to the main pointer only. ### Side steps | step | what happens | options | |---|---|---| | `show(sel)` / `hide(sel)` | tweens `--in` to 1 / 0 on every match; your CSS uses `opacity: var(--in)` etc. | `dur` .35 / .28, `stagger` | | `set(sel, changes)` | instant: `{class: '+on -off'}`, `{text: 'Copied'}`, `{'--x': 2}`, `{'data-view': 'room'}`, `{attr: null}` removes | | | `tween(sel, prop, from, to)` | animates a CSS variable, `'text'` (with `fmt`) or `'scrollTop'` | `dur` .45, `fmt`, `stagger` | | `zoom(sel, z)` | camera pushes in on the target. `z` a number, or `'fit'` to frame the element at `fill` of the frame | `dur` 1.3, `fill` .66 (or `[wide, stacked]`, e.g. `[.76, .96]`: tighter on 1:1 and phones, where the window is small), `aim`, `max` 2.6 (the most a `'fit'` may push in: raise it for a big window such as a whole board), `arc` 0 (0–1: pull back by that share mid-flight and push in again, so a long pan reads as a camera crossing; `demo/canvas`) | | `unzoom()` | camera back to the whole window | `dur` 1.3 | | `chapter(n, title, line)` | the card: `'02 / 05'`, a title with one `` word, one line; until the next chapter | `until` | | `caption(text)` | the caption line, until the next caption | `dur` 4 | | `mark(name)` | nothing on screen: a named moment. `tour.api.marks` lists them in order (`{ t, name }`) and `marks[name]` is that moment's time, so a page can seek to one or stop at the next (`demo/chat`'s beats, `demo/mcp`'s tabs) | | `show`, `hide` and `tween` take `ease`: `'out'` (decelerate), `'ios'` (a critically damped spring, UIKit's pushes and sheets), `'spring'` (overshoots by about 3 %), `'linear'`, or any `(t) => t` function. The default is smootherstep. The curves are exported as `eases`. `data-tour-follow` on a scrolling element (a terminal, a chat thread, a log) keeps its newest content in view every frame, so lines that `stream()` in push the old ones up. `data-tour-grow` on an element that should take height as it arrives (a message in a thread, a folded panel): the engine measures its natural height into `--h` (design px, innermost first, before targets are measured, and again on every relayout), so your CSS can open it with `--in` and let go once it's in: `max-height: max(calc(var(--in) * var(--h)), calc((var(--in) - .999) * 1e7px))`. Rows arrive smoothly and may change size afterwards. `../_chat/chat.css` is the worked example. Elements that `show()` controls should start hidden in CSS (`--in: 0`). Anything the script changes is reset when you seek backwards, because every value is recomputed from `t`. ### The camera `zoom` pushes in on a point and keeps the window filling the frame: it borrows Monet Shot's fit clamp, so a push-in never pans past the window's edge (the window is either wholly inside the frame or covers it). Zoom levels move on a log scale, so in and out feel even. Numbers are multiplied by 1.15 on portrait stages, where the window is small (not inside a `data-tour-frame`, which the window always fills). `?camera=off` turns all push-ins off. On stacked stages (1:1, 9:16, phones) the cursor fades out rather than being drawn outside the window's frame. ### Measuring Targets are measured in the window's own pixels, against the product as it is at the moment each step happens (so a button inside a modal that opens two steps earlier is measured with the modal open), and measured again whenever the layout can change: fonts loading, the stage resizing, your CSS. Edit the product freely; the script follows. ## The card and caption keep out of the way The chapter card and the caption never sit on what the tour is doing. Each frame the engine checks the cursor (or fingertip) and any text being typed (`type`) or streamed in (`stream`), with its last second after. If the card would cover it, the card slides to the other side of the stage; if both sides are busy it steps out, and it comes home once the spot has been clear for .8 s. The caption lifts to the top. Outside `?record` the card carries a × that hides the cards for the rest of the visit; recordings have none. Nothing to configure. In stacked layouts (phones, 9:16) the card already sits under the window, so nothing moves. ## Drivers | driver | how | when | |---|---|---| | `scroll` (default) | `data-driver="scroll"`. The section gets tall, the stage pins, scroll maps to `t`. The gate starts an auto-play drift at real speed. With `data-lock` (default on) wheel, touch and keys can't skip the film while it drifts; the Auto-play switch is the way out. A film at the very top of the page holds the page still until the first click, tap or key. | the opening of a launch page, Monet Shot style | | `play` | `data-driver="play"`. A 100svh stage with a play button, a scrubber with chapter ticks and a timecode. Space or K plays, arrows step 3 s. | a film in the middle of a page | | `manual` | `data-driver="manual"` (or `new Tour(root, script, { driver: 'manual' })`). # AGENT.md: write this product's launch note for the feature it just shipped You are a coding agent inside a team's product repository. They picked this format: the "we just shipped it" changelog post for **one** feature. A short headline and the date; a 10–20 second loop of just that feature, a scripted cursor clicking through the real screen; the screen before and after under a draggable line; three short notes on what changed; the update command. Calm, editorial, quick to make: an afternoon, not a week. Opened with `?record&ratio=16:9` the loop becomes a short film (headline card, the loop once, an update card) to record for the X post. Read `tour/README.md` once for the engine's vocabulary. Then work through this in order. ## 0. Where things are ``` index.html the page. Its markup is yours to edit: the note (
: header, the loop, before/after, notes), then the install card (
) kit/ placeholder kit: tokens, .ph frames, buttons, notes (press N to hide notes) launch-note/script.js the loop's script launch-note/section.css the note's layout, the recording layouts, and the placeholder product's CSS (.ln-app …) launch-note/section.js starts the loop when it's on screen; the before/after divider tour/ the engine (tour.js, tour.css), snapshot.py, README.md; don't edit install/ the end card: name, the update commands, footer ``` (In the StyleFeatures repo, `python3 templates/scaffolds/sections/demo/tour/export.py --format launch-note` makes this layout.) Serve the folder with any static server, e.g. `python3 -m http.server 8000`. ## 1. Find the feature (10 minutes) Take it from what actually shipped, newest first: ```sh gh pr list --state merged --limit 15 --json number,title,mergedAt,url # the latest merged PRs gh pr view --json title,body,files,mergedAt,url,labels # the one you pick git log --oneline --since="3 weeks ago" --no-merges # if they don't use PRs git describe --tags --abbrev=0; gh release view --json tagName,publishedAt,body # the release it's in sed -n 1,60p CHANGELOG.md # if they keep one ``` Pick **one user-facing feature** (not a refactor, not a dependency bump, not three small fixes). From the PR, the commits and the code it touches, write down: - **Headline**: the feature's name, then what it does, in under ten words; one phrase in italics (``). "Filters, on every list", not "Introducing our powerful new filtering experience". - **Date**: when it reached people (the release or merge date), in ``. - **Version**: the tag it ships in. Delete the field if they don't version. - **Dek**: one or two sentences: who it's for and the moment it helps. - **Three notes**: what's new; what it replaces or fixes; what people need to do (often: nothing). - **The source**: the PR or release link, only if the repository is public. Otherwise delete the line. Never invent numbers, quotes, customers or benchmarks. If the PR says "2× faster" and shows how, you may say it; if it doesn't, don't. ## 2. Harvest the screen, twice The feature lives on one screen. You need that screen in two states, at the same size: - **before**: the base branch or the last release, without the feature; - **after**: this branch, with it. Run both side by side with a worktree, seeded with the same demo data (fixtures, a seed script, a demo account; never real customer data): ```sh git worktree add ../before origin/main # or the previous tag (cd ../before && && ) uv run tour/snapshot.py http://localhost:3001/tasks --selector "#root" --size 1200x710 --out launch-note/fragments/before.html --scope before uv run tour/snapshot.py http://localhost:3000/tasks --selector "#root" --size 1200x710 --out launch-note/fragments/after.html --scope after ``` `--size` is the window's size minus the browser bar (750 − 40). Use `--before "js"` to reach a state (open a menu, apply the filter) and `--hook "css=name"` to mark what the loop's cursor will click. Capture each state the loop needs as its own fragment too (`--scope` unique per fragment). - **Before/after**: replace the two empty panes in `index.html` with the fragments: `
` (paths are relative to `index.html`). Filled panes are left alone; the placeholder's clone step and its `STATES` in `section.js` can go. - **The loop's window**: replace `.ln-app` with the fragments for each state, stacked, switched with `show()`/`hide()` at the click that causes them; small changes (a checkbox, a count, a chip) are better done with `set`/`tween` on hooks. Keep `data-chrome="browser"` for a web app (`data-url` its real path), `app` for a desktop app; for a mobile feature use the `demo/phone` format's window and `pointer: 'touch'`. - A native app can't be snapshotted: rebuild the screen from its views in static HTML/CSS with their exact tokens, icons and strings (see `demo/phone`'s AGENT.md for the method), once per state. ## 3. Write the loop (`launch-note/script.js`) - **10–20 seconds, three to five actions, one feature.** Start on the state people already know, end on the result. Every click visibly changes something. - **Two zooms at most**: one on the control, one on the result. `unzoom()` before the end so the loop's seam is the whole window. - **A caption per action**, a short sentence in the product's voice. The loop plays muted. - `still` is the frame reduced motion shows: the result, with its caption. - `intro` and `outro` already differ for recordings (a headline card and an update card) and the page (a breath before it starts again); leave them unless the loop feels rushed. ## 4. Check it - `index.html?t=6` freezes a moment: check one just after each click and at each zoom (the cursor on its target, the thing that changed in view). - Let it play: it starts when it scrolls into view, pauses off screen, and the pause button wins. The film's own camera does the push-ins; use `&camera=off` if you'd rather add zooms on Monet Shot's timeline. 3. Export H.264 MP4 (X: up to 2 min 20 s, 512 MB; this is 15–25 s). 16:9 for desktop and quote posts; record `ratio=1:1` separately for a phone-first feed. 4. Post one line ("Filters, on every list.") and the link to this note.

# tour.js: the demo-film engine One engine for every StyleFeatures demo film. A template supplies a window with a product inside it and a script; the engine plays it with a fake cursor, a camera, chapter cards and captions, and drives it from a scroll, a clock, a screen recorder or a frozen `?t=`. Files: | file | what it is | edit it? | |---|---|---| | `tour.js` | the engine: step builders, `Tour`, `include()` | no, it's shared by every format | | `tour.css` | the engine's look: chromes, cursor, card, caption, keys, controls, record stage | no; restyle through its tokens | | `script.js` | this film's script | yes | | `section.html` / `section.css` | this film's band, closing frame and product | yes | | `snapshot.py` | harvests a live screen into a static fragment | no | | `export.py` | copies the whole format out as a standalone folder | no | | `AGENT.md` | the brief for the coding agent that fills it in | read it | Everything on screen is a pure function of one number, `t`, in seconds. Each frame the engine works out the product's state at `t` (classes, attributes, text, CSS variables, scroll positions), the camera, the cursor and the overlays, then writes only what changed. Nothing depends on what happened in earlier frames, so any moment renders on its own, the same way every time. ## Markup ```html
… your product, built at 1200 × 750 design pixels …
…
…
``` The engine adds the chrome, the cursor, ripples, the chapter card, the caption line, key caps, and the driver's controls. The opening band (`data-tour-band`) slides away in the first `intro` seconds; the closing frame (`data-tour-end`) gets `--in` 0→1 at the end and its own CSS decides what that looks like. The root also carries `--tour-band` (1 → 0 over the intro), `--tour-out` (0 → 1 over the outro) and `--tour-p` (0 → 1 over the whole film) for a format's own CSS. `data-tour-band="css"` stops the engine sliding the band away; the format fades or moves it from `--tour-band` instead. **A frame the format draws: `data-tour-frame`.** Put an element with `data-tour-frame` in the stage and lay it out in CSS (a phone's glass, a mat around a screenshot, a different box per ratio). The engine fits the window to it exactly, clips the camera to it (with its `border-radius`), and every zoom stays inside it: the window always covers the frame, so a push-in never shows what's around it. The outro then leaves the window where it is (use `--tour-out` to do something else). Give the frame the window's aspect ratio. `demo/phone` (the glass, beside the text or under it) and `demo/launch-note` (a mat on the page, a different box per recording ratio) use it. ### Window chromes: `data-chrome` | value | looks like | typical `data-size` | |---|---|---| | `browser` | traffic lights, back/forward, an address pill (`data-url`), share/new icons | `1200x750` | | `app` | a macOS title bar with traffic lights and a centred `data-title` | `1200x760` | | `phone` | a dark bezel, a status bar with the time and a notch | `390x844` | | `none` | just rounded corners | anything | | `terminal` | a warm charcoal window, traffic lights, a centred `data-title`; tokens `--tour-term-bg/-bar/-ink/-dim` | `780x548` | **Windows inside the window.** Any element inside the window with a `data-chrome` gets that chrome too, and a frame (`display:flex`, rounded, clipped). With `data-chrome="none"` on the outer window (made transparent in your CSS) it becomes a desk holding, say, a terminal and a browser; the camera pans between them with `zoom()` (`demo/terminal` does this). **A second design size for tall stages.** `data-size-tall="440x820"` on the window (or `sizeTall: [440, 820]` in the script) is used whenever the stage is taller than wide (W/H < .8: phones, 9:16 recordings). The root gets `.is-tall` before anything is measured, so your CSS can re-lay the product for it (stack two panes, say) and the script's targets follow. `demo/split` stacks its panes this way. **A third for squarish stages.** `data-size-square="760x760"` (or `sizeSquare: [760, 760]`) is used when .8 ≤ W/H < 1.15 (1:1 recordings, square-ish windows), and the root gets `.is-square` the same way. Without it those stages use the wide size, as before. `demo/agentic` has all three: a tiled desk (wide), and one live window beside (square) or above (tall) its run sheet. **A height that follows the frame: `auto`.** `data-size="580xauto"` (or `size: [580, 'auto']`, and the same for `sizeTall`) fixes the window's width and takes its height from the `data-tour-frame` at every layout, so the window always has the frame's shape: a full-height column on a wide page, the whole screen on a phone, any recording ratio. For products that read top to bottom (a chat, a feed, a transcript). `demo/chat` and `demo/mcp` use it. Build the product at the design size in plain CSS pixels. The engine scales the whole window, so text stays real text and stays sharp at any zoom. ### Hooks `'@name'` anywhere in a selector means `[data-tour="name"]`. Put `data-tour="…"` on the things the script points at. Pointer targets also choose the cursor: links, buttons, `role=button|tab|switch` get the hand, inputs and `data-tour-cursor="text"` get the I-beam, the rest the arrow (`data-tour-cursor="arrow|pointer|text"` overrides it). While the cursor rests on a target, that target has `.is-hover`; while it's pressed, `.is-press`. Style both so clicks read. ## The script ```js import { click, type, show, hide, set, tween, zoom, unzoom, chapter, caption, pause } from './tour.js'; export default { size: [1200, 750], // window design size (or data-size on the window) enter: [.84, .97], // where the cursor comes in from, as fractions of the window intro: 1.3, // seconds for the opening band to clear (0: no band) outro: 4.5, // seconds held on the closing frame settle: .6, // pause between the last step and the outro still: 17.4, // the moment reduced motion shows fit: [.92, .88, .5], // optional: see below steps: [ … ], }; ``` `fit: [w, h, y]` is for a stage that holds nothing but the window (a panel beside text, with no card or band over it): the window may take `w` of the stage's width and `h` of its height, centred at `y` (default .5), and push-ins aim at the middle of the frame. Without it the page layout leaves room for the card and band (`[.74, .7, .47]`). It never changes `?record`. `demo/chapters` uses it. Steps run in order on one clock. **Pointer steps** take time and the next step waits for them. **Side steps** start at the current moment and the next step starts with them, so `click('@create'), hide('@modal'), show('@toast')` hides the modal and shows the toast as the click lands. Every step takes: `at: 12.5` pin it to an absolute time · `wait: .4` start this much later · `parallel: true` (pointer steps) don't hold up the next step · `block: true` (side steps) do hold it up. ### Pointer steps | step | what happens | options (defaults) | |---|---|---| | `move(sel)` | glides there on a gentle arc, smootherstep | `dur` .9, `aim` [x, y] fractions of the target, `cursor` | | `click(sel)` | moves, presses (cursor shrinks, target gets `.is-press`), ripple | as `move` | | `dblclick(sel)` | moves, two presses, two ripples | as `move` | | `hover(sel)` | moves and rests (`.is-hover` on the target) | `dur` .9, `hold` .6 | | `type(sel, text)` | characters appear in `sel` at a human, uneven pace; `.is-caret` while typing, then blinking | `cps` 13, `rhythm` (below), `lead` (s of steady caret before the first key), `caret` (s it blinks after the last key, 1.6), `blink` (absolute time it goes) | | `stream(sel)` | each match appears in turn, like output arriving: gets `.is-in`, and `--in` 0→1 over `dur`. A match's `data-tour-wait="1.2"` adds that pause before it (a slow step) | `every` .06 s, `jitter` .5 (±50 % of `every`; 0 for an exact beat), `dur` .08 | | `drag(handle, o)` | moves to the handle, presses, then drives a value while the cursor stays on the handle | `approach` .8, `dur` 1.2, `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el` to put the property on another element), `text: [sel, v => label]`, or `onto: sel` to carry the handle itself there | | `scroll(sel, to)` | scrolls an element; `to` is px, `'50%'`, `'end'` or a selector inside it | `dur` 1.4, `offset` 16 | | `key(keys)` | key caps on screen, e.g. `key(['⌘', 'K'])` | `dur` .9, `hold` 1.4 | | `pause(s)` | a beat | | | `tap(sel)` | the same step as `click`; reads better in a touch film | as `click` | | `longpress(sel)` | moves, presses and holds; it fires (`.is-press` stays on, a ripple) after `hold`, and the finger stays down `lift` longer while the next steps start (open a context menu there) | `dur` .9, `hold` .7, `lift` .35 | | `swipe(sel, o)` | a finger flick that starts on `sel`: lands, travels `by` [dx, dy] window px speeding up, lifts while still moving. What it moves follows it 1:1, then coasts to rest over `coast` s with the speed it was let go at. `scroll: to` scrolls `sel` (or `in: sel`) to `to` (px, `'50%'`, `'end'`, a selector; `offset`); `prop` + `from` + `to` (+ `el`) drives a CSS variable instead (a carousel, a sheet dragged down), `follow` (.45) of it under the finger | `approach` .7, `by` [0, -220], `dur` .36, `coast` .8 (0: a slow drag that ends at rest), `settle` (when the next step starts, `coast` × .5) | `type`'s `rhythm`: unset is the even, slightly uneven pace it always had. `'human'` types like a person at a keyboard: a beat between words, a reach for symbols (`- / . : =`), a pause after punctuation, doubled letters run together, the odd hesitation. `'stream'` lands the text in chunks of 1–5 characters, the way a model's reply arrives. `stream()` is for whole lines or blocks; hide them in CSS until `.is-in` (`.line{display:none}.line.is-in{display:block}`) so they take space only once they've arrived. The cursor's path between targets is a smootherstep glide with a slight bow (direction-dependent, never a straight line) and a slightly early peak speed, like a hand. It never teleports: each move starts where the last one ended. **A finger instead of a cursor.** `pointer: 'touch'` in the script (or `data-pointer="touch"` on the root, `?pointer=touch`) swaps the arrow for a fingertip: a soft translucent dot, 44 window px, that is part of the screen, so it zooms with it. It is unseen between touches (a hand travelling isn't on the glass); a shadow gathers for a fifth of a second before contact, the dot flattens and darkens while pressed (`.is-down` on `.tour-cur`), and lifts away. `drag` and `swipe` carry it across the glass. Give each touch a beat: the `dur` before it is the hand travelling. Restyle the dot with `--tour-touch` / `--tour-touch-down`. `demo/phone` is the worked example. **More than one pointer.** Any pointer step with `by: 'agent'` moves a second cursor on its own track (any name works; steps without `by` move the usual one, `'main'`). Describe each in the script: ```js pointers: { main: { label: 'You', idle: 1.4 }, // a tag on the person's cursor; it fades after 1.4 s still agent: { label: 'Agent', look: 'agent', bow: .2, enter: [.33, .2] }, }, steps: [ click('@search', { by: 'agent', tag: 'search_code' }), …, click('@approve', { from: [.99, 1.03] }) ] ``` A second pointer is an arrow in `--tour-agent` (look `'agent'`) with a label tag beside it; `tag` on a step adds a word to that label from then on (the tool it's using, "waiting for you"). `bow` scales the curve of its path (0 is a straight, machine-like line), `enter` is where it first appears, `shapes: true` lets it take the hand and I-beam too. `idle: s` fades a pointer out once it has been still that long and back in when it next moves; `from: [x, y]` (fractions of the window) on a step starts that move there instead, so a hand can come back in from off the edge. Each pointer's clicks ripple in its own colour (`.tour-ring[data-who]`), and `.tour-cur[data-who="…"]` lets a page hide one (`demo/agentic` hides the person's cursor on the live page, where the visitor is the person). Touch mode (`pointer: 'touch'`) applies to the main pointer only. ### Side steps | step | what happens | options | |---|---|---| | `show(sel)` / `hide(sel)` | tweens `--in` to 1 / 0 on every match; your CSS uses `opacity: var(--in)` etc. | `dur` .35 / .28, `stagger` | | `set(sel, changes)` | instant: `{class: '+on -off'}`, `{text: 'Copied'}`, `{'--x': 2}`, `{'data-view': 'room'}`, `{attr: null}` removes | | | `tween(sel, prop, from, to)` | animates a CSS variable, `'text'` (with `fmt`) or `'scrollTop'` | `dur` .45, `fmt`, `stagger` | | `zoom(sel, z)` | camera pushes in on the target. `z` a number, or `'fit'` to frame the element at `fill` of the frame | `dur` 1.3, `fill` .66 (or `[wide, stacked]`, e.g. `[.76, .96]`: tighter on 1:1 and phones, where the window is small), `aim`, `max` 2.6 (the most a `'fit'` may push in: raise it for a big window such as a whole board), `arc` 0 (0–1: pull back by that share mid-flight and push in again, so a long pan reads as a camera crossing; `demo/canvas`) | | `unzoom()` | camera back to the whole window | `dur` 1.3 | | `chapter(n, title, line)` | the card: `'02 / 05'`, a title with one `` word, one line; until the next chapter | `until` | | `caption(text)` | the caption line, until the next caption | `dur` 4 | | `mark(name)` | nothing on screen: a named moment. `tour.api.marks` lists them in order (`{ t, name }`) and `marks[name]` is that moment's time, so a page can seek to one or stop at the next (`demo/chat`'s beats, `demo/mcp`'s tabs) | | `show`, `hide` and `tween` take `ease`: `'out'` (decelerate), `'ios'` (a critically damped spring, UIKit's pushes and sheets), `'spring'` (overshoots by about 3 %), `'linear'`, or any `(t) => t` function. The default is smootherstep. The curves are exported as `eases`. `data-tour-follow` on a scrolling element (a terminal, a chat thread, a log) keeps its newest content in view every frame, so lines that `stream()` in push the old ones up. `data-tour-grow` on an element that should take height as it arrives (a message in a thread, a folded panel): the engine measures its natural height into `--h` (design px, innermost first, before targets are measured, and again on every relayout), so your CSS can open it with `--in` and let go once it's in: `max-height: max(calc(var(--in) * var(--h)), calc((var(--in) - .999) * 1e7px))`. Rows arrive smoothly and may change size afterwards. `../_chat/chat.css` is the worked example. Elements that `show()` controls should start hidden in CSS (`--in: 0`). Anything the script changes is reset when you seek backwards, because every value is recomputed from `t`. ### The camera `zoom` pushes in on a point and keeps the window filling the frame: it borrows Monet Shot's fit clamp, so a push-in never pans past the window's edge (the window is either wholly inside the frame or covers it). Zoom levels move on a log scale, so in and out feel even. Numbers are multiplied by 1.15 on portrait stages, where the window is small (not inside a `data-tour-frame`, which the window always fills). `?camera=off` turns all push-ins off. On stacked stages (1:1, 9:16, phones) the cursor fades out rather than being drawn outside the window's frame. ### Measuring Targets are measured in the window's own pixels, against the product as it is at the moment each step happens (so a button inside a modal that opens two steps earlier is measured with the modal open), and measured again whenever the layout can change: fonts loading, the stage resizing, your CSS. Edit the product freely; the script follows. ## The card and caption keep out of the way The chapter card and the caption never sit on what the tour is doing. Each frame the engine checks the cursor (or fingertip) and any text being typed (`type`) or streamed in (`stream`), with its last second after. If the card would cover it, the card slides to the other side of the stage; if both sides are busy it steps out, and it comes home once the spot has been clear for .8 s. The caption lifts to the top. Outside `?record` the card carries a × that hides the cards for the rest of the visit; recordings have none. Nothing to configure. The film may sit anywhere in the page, inside another section: everything that isn't the film or one of its ancestors is hidden. It holds the first frame (the title band), plays once from 0 and stops on the closing frame. Captions are on, because X autoplays muted. Record it with **Monet Shot**: pick the browser window, crop to the stage, and export. Two things to know: - Monet Shot zooms on **real** clicks. The tour's clicks are drawn, not real, so Monet Shot sees none and adds no zooms of its own. The tour's camera therefore stays **on** by default. If you would rather place zooms yourself on Monet Shot's timeline, use `&camera=off` and you won't get double zooms. - Monet Shot draws its own cursor from the real pointer. Park the real pointer off the recorded window (or set Monet Shot's cursor to hidden) so only the tour's cursor shows. From script: `window.tour` has `seek(t)`, `play()`, `pause()`, `load(script)`, `t`, `duration`, `chapters` and `ready` (a promise that resolves once fonts are in and everything is measured). The root gets a `tour:end` event whenever `play()` reaches the end (any driver). **Several tours in one recorded frame.** A format whose recording is more than one film (two windows racing in `demo/versus`, a whole slide deck in `demo/deck`) makes its own element the record stage and drives the tours itself: ```js import { Tour, recordStage } from './tour.js'; const box = q.has('record') ? recordStage(root) : null; // root becomes the ratio's box, centred on near-black, the rest hidden const a = new Tour(filmA, scriptA, { driver: 'manual', record: 'page' }); // no record stage or auto-play of its own a.render(t); // the page decides t, every frame ``` `recordStage(el)` does for `el` what `?record` does for a single film (the `tour-record` and `sf-clean` classes, `--rw`/`--rh` from `&ratio=`, kept current on resize) and returns `{ w, h, ratio }`. `{ record: 'page' }` on a Tour means: in `?record` stay on the manual driver and let the page play it (captions follow `captions` as usual). Without `?record` it changes nothing. The page then holds the first frame, plays once and honours `&t=` itself. `load(script)` swaps in another script on the same window: every value the old script touched goes back to how the page drew it, then the new script is compiled and measured. `demo/playground` uses it to turn a visitor's clicks into a live script that the engine plays on from, so their clicks get the film's eases. ## Harvested screens: `include()` and `snapshot.py` ```html
